title: Boxer Rebellion
summary: The Boxer uprising began in northern China as the Yihetuan, a secret society, took up arms in 1898 and 1899 against foreigners, Christian missionaries and Chinese Christian converts. The 55-day siege of the foreign legations in Beijing in 1900 prompted an eight-nation alliance to send a 20,000-strong force that relieved them. The settlement required China to pay an indemnity of 450 million taels of silver.

uncertainty.note: Rural attacks began in 1898–1899 in Shandong; siege of legations and international intervention culminated in 1900–1901.

importance.justification: The Boxer Rebellion and its harsh settlement weakened the Qing imperial government, accelerating the internal political breakdown that led to the 1911 Revolution.

audience_note: Addresses violent conflict, the targeting and killing of missionaries and Chinese Christian converts, and punitive reprisals and looting by allied forces.

related.because: Unequal treaties and foreign concessions imposed after the Opium Wars generated widespread anti-foreign resentment that fueled the Boxer uprising.
The devastating Boxer Protocol indemnity and foreign military occupation fatally undermined the authority of the Qing dynasty, precipitating the 1911 revolution.

sources.title: The Boxer Uprising - I: The Gathering Storm
